why: This checker's default run is over assets that are all correct, so nothing about it going quiet shows up in an exit code: a requirement table emptied, a dimension comparison that no longer fires, a missing file read as a pass — every one of those leaves the run printing the same clean line. The self-test breaks a generated asset tree one way at a time and requires a refusal each time, and the edits below are the ways the checker could stop being able to refuse anything.

mutations.name: the SVG requirements are never checked
mutations.breaks: The ketu mark, wordmark, compact mark and architecture diagram stop being checked for a viewBox or a title, which is how an asset ends up shipping under the wrong name.
mutations.find:
for relative, expected_title in SVG_REQUIREMENTS.items():
        problems.extend(validate_svg(root, relative, expected_title))
mutations.replace:
for relative, expected_title in []:
        problems.extend(validate_svg(root, relative, expected_title))

mutations.name: the PNG requirement table is emptied
mutations.breaks: The checker is disabled by deleting its input rather than its code — the shape of failure that reads as a clean run over nothing.

mutations.name: the PNG parse returns the answer it was expected to give
mutations.breaks: The file is never read: the checker compares the requirement with itself and agrees. This is the edit that would survive every check downstream of it, including the byte flipped with its CRC re-signed.

mutations.name: the problems are printed and the run exits 0
mutations.breaks: The checker finds everything and reports it, and the exit code says the tree is fine. Nothing that reads only the verdict would ever know.
